extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies and planners preparing state plans under CAA section 111(d) (particularly for fossil-fuel-fired steam generating EGUs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how a state must demonstrate that a particular affected EGU (or class of EGUs) cannot reasonably achieve the EPA's presumptive degree of emission limitation or compliance schedule (i.e., invoking Remaining Useful Life or Function — RULOF) and how to calculate any less-stringent standard or longer compliance schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: State burden to document/justify standards of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: States carry the burden of making any demonstrations in support of less-stringent standards of performance pursuant to RULOF in developing their plans; the EPA must be able to ascertain, based on the information and analysis included in the state plan submission, that the standard meets statutory and regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must reasonably document and justify standards of performance in their plans; submissions should include sufficient information and analysis for EPA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for invoking RULOF (40 CFR 60.24a(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A state may apply a less stringent standard of performance or longer compliance schedule only if it demonstrates that the facility cannot reasonably achieve the EPA's degree of emission limitation based on one or more enumerated circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enumerated circumstances are: (1) unreasonable cost resulting from plant age, location, or basic process design; (2) physical impossibility or technical infeasibility of installing necessary control equipment; (3) other factors specific to the facility. The state must show fundamental differences between the facility-specific information and the information the EPA considered in the emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on presumptive rate-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: For these emission guidelines the EPA provides presumptive standards of performance in the form of rate-based emission limitations; the relevant consideration for RULOF is whether the affected EGU can reasonably achieve the applicable rate-based presumptive standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should evaluate whether an EGU can meet the EPA's rate-based standard rather than whether it can implement an abstract BSER; analyses should target the rate-based metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific cost and performance evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA considered costs in terms of $/ton CO2 reduced and $/MWh increase in levelized costs; non-air quality health and environmental impacts and energy requirements were considered in terms of parasitic load and boiler efficiency and other metrics specific to systems evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should, where possible, use the same metrics ($/ton CO2 reduced and $/MWh) to compare unit-specific costs to EPA's baseline, though they may consider additional metrics if justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cost as objective, replicable metric where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, states should reflect source-specific considerations in terms of cost, because cost is an objective and replicable metric for comparison to EPA's information and across affected EGUs and states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: pipeline length considerations are best reflected through pipeline cost; remaining useful life effects should be expressed via annualized costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of remaining useful life via annualized costs
rubrics_metrics.description: When invoking RULOF based on remaining useful life, a state must demonstrate that the annualized costs of applying the EPA's BSER degree of emission limitation for a source with a short remaining useful life are fundamentally different from the costs the EPA found reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For annualized cost calculations the EPA considers the amortization period to begin at the compliance date for the applicable subcategory; remaining useful life affects capital recovery and thus annualized costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental-difference standard (unit-specific vs EPA baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: States must demonstrate that the facility-specific information is fundamentally different from the information the EPA considered in the emission guidelines in a way that makes achieving the degree of limitation or compliance schedule unreasonable for that facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The “fundamental difference” must be shown with supporting documentation and cannot be mere speculation; EPA examples are illustrative, not bright-line rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of EPA BSER cost values (no bright-line threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA BSER cost values are typically fleet averages; those averages are not bright-line thresholds separating reasonable from unreasonable unit-specific costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some unit-specific costs above the average may still be reasonable; EPA is not setting generally-applicable numerical thresholds in these guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example cost benchmarks (illustrative guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA gave illustrative numerical examples: e.g., $71/ton CO2 reduced and $13/MWh for co-firing, $18.50/MWh for installation of wet-FGD on a 300 MW unit; costs greater than the 95th percentile on a fleetwide basis might indicate an outlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA clarifies these are examples only—not mandatory thresholds. A cost above the 95th percentile could be valid evidence of a fundamental difference but is not the only way to demonstrate one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for 'other factors specific to the facility'
rubrics_metrics.description: States may invoke RULOF based on other factors not considered by EPA or additional evaluation metrics, but must demonstrate such factors make it unreasonable for the affected EGU to achieve the EPA's degree of emission limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'other factors' can be categories of information EPA did not consider or different ways of evaluating a category; states must tie such factors causally to unreasonableness of meeting the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoking RULOF for a class of facilities—similarity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: RULOF may be invoked for a class of facilities only where all facilities in the class are similarly situated in all meaningful ways relevant to the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The class must share not only the circumstance that is the basis for RULOF but also other relevant characteristics (size, process, footprint, location, etc.). EPA expects it would be unlikely reasonable to invoke RULOF for a class under these guidelines because affected EGUs are typically heterogeneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF cannot change subcategory structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Invocation of RULOF does not modify the EPA's subcategory structure or create a new subcategory; the affected EGU remains in the subcategory for which the presumptive standard applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any particularized compliance obligations must differ as little as possible from the presumptive standard and schedule for that subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term coal EGUs — CCS-specific evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: If considering CCS, states should evaluate whether the EGU's circumstances are fundamentally different from the CCS-specific information EPA considered (capture costs; CO2 transport and sequestration costs; availability of IRC section 45Q tax credit; capacity factor assumptions; water use; capture plant siting; transport and geologic sequestration; parasitic/auxiliary energy demand; net power output decreases; energy sector impacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a state asserts physical impossibility or technical infeasibility for CCS at an EGU, it must demonstrate fundamental differences from the EPA's CCS information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal EGUs — natural gas co-firing metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For co-firing, relevant EPA-considered metrics include costs of adding new gas burners and boiler modifications, fuel cost, new natural gas pipelines, losses in boiler efficiency, non-GHG emissions, and impacts on energy sector structure and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may also consider other relevant factors and must show any claimed fundamental differences in such metrics compared to EPA's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for providing a longer compliance schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a longer compliance schedule via RULOF, the state must demonstrate a fundamental difference between the EPA's subcategory-level information and the particular EGU's circumstances, substantiated with documentation supporting and justifying why implementation will take longer than EPA considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances should not be speculative; if a process will take longer than typical/historical, the state should explain why and provide corroborating evidence. The source-specific compliance date must be no later than necessary and as close as reasonably possible to the standard schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of best efforts as support for longer schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary evidence (receipts, invoices, actual site work) that a source is making best endeavors to achieve compliance as expeditiously as possible is strong support for granting a longer compliance schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should show that the need for extra time exists notwithstanding best efforts; EPA does not preclude other types of reasonable evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for calculating less-stringent standard (40 CFR 60.24a(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the state demonstrates an EGU cannot reasonably achieve the EPA's degree of emission limitation, the state must determine a standard of performance or schedule that is no less stringent/no longer than necessary to address the fundamental difference, using the process in 40 CFR 60.24a(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That process involves evaluating, to the extent necessary, the systems of emission reduction the EPA identified in the guidelines using the same factors and evaluation metrics the Agency used. The resulting standard must be as close to EPA's degree of limitation or schedule as reasonably possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: When evaluation of other systems may not be necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If an EGU is implementing the BSER but cannot achieve the degree of emission limitation due to fundamental differences, the state may not need to evaluate other systems of emission reduction; instead it can determine the degree the EGU can reasonably achieve as the basis for the less-stringent standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if capture equipment can reasonably achieve 85% capture but not 90%, and no other system could enable 90%, the state may set a standard corresponding to 85% without further evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA review standard for state RULOF analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will assess each use of RULOF in a state plan against the applicable regulatory requirements (40 CFR 60.24a(e)-(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should structure submissions so EPA can determine compliance with these regulatory provisions; many comments on the scope of EPA review were outside the scope of this rulemaking but EPA reserves review authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for additional cost metrics with justification
rubrics_metrics.description: States are expected to evaluate costs using the same metrics EPA used ($/ton CO2 reduced and $/MWh) but may present additional cost metrics if they justify their relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should explain why additional metrics are appropriate and how they inform whether the unit-specific costs are fundamentally different from EPA's baseline.
